fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Social Media Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey, its logic, and the table behind it from one prompt, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written around your platforms

Name the apps you post on and the change the answers should settle. Emergent drafts questions that list each app by name, and a short prompt rewords one or swaps a choice.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer kept as a row you own

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, with the date and the place the link was shared. Run the survey again next spring and both rounds sit in one table.
fields.feature_3:
One tap per screen from a profile link

Followers who tap the link in a bio or a story get one question per screen on a phone, with large answer buttons. Nobody has to pinch and zoom on a long page to finish it.
fields.feature_4:
A follow-up only when the answer calls for it

A yes on the first question can open a second one that asks which post did it. The results page shows a count for each answer, and a filter keeps one group of answers in view.
fields.feature_5:
Opted-in followers sent to your email tool

Followers who check the box for news are sent with their answers to your email tool or CRM through its API. The store can then write only to people who asked for how-to videos.
fields.feature_6:
A short link on your own domain

Put the survey on your own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Social Media Surveys at Work
fields.tab_content_1:
The class schedule, on the app 196 members open first

Fernhook Yoga puts one question in its weekly class email: which app do you open first each day? Of 420 members who answered, 196 picked Instagram and 118 Facebook. TikTok drew 64, and 42 open none of them. The studio now posts its class schedule to Instagram each week and pauses its TikTok account.
fields.tab_content_2:
How-to videos on deck stain, twice a week

Copper Ash Hardware puts a survey link in its Instagram bio that asks which kind of post followers would save. How-to videos drew 612 of 1,340 picks, ahead of sale alerts at 401. New arrivals took 214 and behind the counter 113. The store now films a how-to video twice a week, and deck stain comes first.
fields.tab_content_3:
No more 7 am posts for the next stop

A QR code on the Pepper Line Tacos window asks customers one question while they wait: when do you check social media? Of 860 answers, 344 chose 7 to 9 pm and 278 chose lunch. Mornings drew 160 and late night 78. The truck now posts the next day's stop at 8 pm instead of 7 am.
fields.tab_content_4:
A 20-second video for each adoptable dog

Stillwater Paws Rescue ends every adoption application with one question: did a social media post bring you here? Of 510 applicants, 306 said yes, and only they get a follow-up on which post. Pet videos drew 189 of the 306, photo posts 84, and event posts 33. Each adoptable dog now gets a 20-second video.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Social Media Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write questions for social media survey takers that settle one posting decision, then build the survey with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Before drafting a question, finish one sentence: the answers will decide which app gets the schedule posts, or what time the next post goes up. Put that sentence in your prompt to Emergent, and drop any question that could not change it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each platform its own choice instead of asking about social media in general, and add None. Members who use no app still count, and a large None tally is a reason to keep the email list going.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Offer time ranges such as 7 to 9 pm instead of words like regularly or sometimes. Two people read a vague word in two different ways, while a range hands you the hour to schedule the post.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write each choice the way it appears in a feed: a 60-second how-to video, a sale alert, a photo of new stock. People pick faster when they can picture the post, and the winner tells you what to make next.
fields.howto_step_5_des: A survey opened from a bio link or a QR code competes with the feed for attention. Keep it to five questions or fewer, and put the one that settles your decision first, so people who quit early still answer it.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Save follow-ups for the right people
fields.howto_step_6_des: Show a second question only when the first answer calls for it, such as which post brought someone in after a yes. Everyone else finishes sooner, and the follow-up counts come only from people who can answer.
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the counts are in, say what you changed in a story, a pinned post, or the next email. Followers who see their answers used have a reason to answer the next survey, and the next round shows whether the change worked.

faq_plan.q: What is a questions for social media survey?
faq_plan.a: A questions for social media survey is a short set of questions about how customers or followers use social media. It asks which apps they open, when they scroll, and which posts they want from you, and the answers show where and when your next posts belong.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a questions for social media survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe your followers, the platforms you use, and the decision the answers should settle, and Emergent's AI survey builder writes the questions, a results page, and the database behind them. Try every question on a phone, change any of them with a prompt, and then share the link.

faq_plan.q: Should questions for social media survey takers include age?
faq_plan.a: Only if you will split the results by it. A bakery that posts the same thing for every age group gains nothing from the question. If you do ask, offer age ranges, add Prefer not to say, and place it last so it never stops someone halfway.

faq_plan.q: What social media survey questions for staff help plan training?
faq_plan.a: Ask which platforms each person posts on for work, have them rate their confidence on each from 1 to 5, and list skills to pick from, such as short video or replying to comments. For a full training needs survey, start from learning and development survey questions.

faq_plan.q: Where should I post social media survey questions for followers?
faq_plan.a: Post them where the people you want to hear from already are. Use a bio link or story for followers, the email list for customers who may not follow you, and a QR code at the counter for walk-ins. However many answers a busy week brings, Emergent puts no response cap on the survey.

faq_plan.q: Should social media survey questions for customers be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for opinion questions about your posts, since people answer more frankly when no name is attached. If you want to follow up, add an optional last question that asks for an email address. Either way, every answer is stored in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Which profile questions for social media survey takers are worth asking?
faq_plan.a: Only the ones that change what you post: why someone follows you, their skill level, or how far they live from your shop. For a fuller picture of the people who show up, start from a set of audience survey questions and add the social media ones.

faq_plan.q: How often should I repeat social media survey questions for my followers?
faq_plan.a: Repeat them once a year, and again after a big change such as a new posting schedule or a new app. Keep the wording identical between rounds. A shift in the counts then reflects your followers, not a reworded question.

faq_plan.q: Can social media survey questions for shoppers show which posts lead to sales?
faq_plan.a: Partly. It shows which posts customers say brought them in, which is their memory, not a tracked click. Ask the question right after a purchase, while the post is fresh. With Emergent, adding that question to an existing survey later takes one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: Which social media survey questions for gaming communities work best?
faq_plan.a: Ask where members watch streams, where they chat between sessions, and which kinds of clips they share with friends. Those answers tell you which platforms deserve your posts. For questions about the games themselves, add a set of game survey questions.

faq_heading: Questions for Social Media Survey FAQ

plan.angle: The SERP for this query is question lists with no context: generic survey examples and post ideas that never say which question settles which decision. This page treats a social media survey as the few questions a small business or nonprofit asks its own customers about their social media habits, and shows four surveys built from a prompt that each end in one change: which app gets the schedule posts, what the next videos cover, what time the next-day post goes up, and which post format every adoptable dog gets. The how-to gives question-writing advice as plain instructions, and the FAQ covers length, staff training, demographics, where to share it, audience profile, anonymity, frequency and gaming communities with no third-party claims.
